subject: MAP Kickoff — GPU pool evaluation & close plan (Novanet)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena@novanet.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@arcadiaai.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Kickoff — GPU pool evaluation & close plan (Novanet)

Hi all,

Thanks for moving quickly on this. Novanet is prioritizing a Dedicated GPU pool to reach consistent throughput for their image-generation workloads and wants a concrete MAP (mutual action plan) that gets to a signed SOW within 6 weeks. I put together an initial MAP workbook (attached) and sketched roles below.

Objective: validate throughput at target QPS and finalize contract terms so Novanet can shift 50k monthly tokens to Redwood Dedicated by mid-June.

Proposed 6-week milestones (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, stakeholder alignment, agree eval criteria and target throughput
- Week 1–2: evaluation runs (baseline -> optimized), collect token/latency metrics, validate caching/kv config
- Week 3: performance regression checks, finalize quantization and batch profile; legal review of SOW
- Week 4–5: pilot on dedicated pool, finalize pricing addendum
- Week 6: executive sign-off and SOW execution

Assigned roles (suggested):
- Redwood PM / owner: Marcus Lin — MAP owner and commercial lead
- Redwood SRE/Infra: Rishi Malhotra — GPU pool sizing, batch/config tuning
- Redwood Customer Success: Monica Patel — onboarding and pilot run oversight
- Redwood Product: Grace O'Connor — perf targets and eval plan
- Redwood Legal/Finance: Laura Bennett — SOW coordination

Action items for this thread: please confirm you can cover the role above and 1) whether the milestones/timeline look OK, 2) what the initial throughput target should be (QPS and latency SLO), and 3) one constraint or risk you want captured in the MAP (e.g., region limits, data residency, procurement lead time).

I've attached: MAP-Dedicated-GPU-2027-05-20.xlsx (workbook) and novanet-SOW-draft-v1.pdf.

I propose a quick 30-min sync today at 10:00 PT — if that doesn't work, flag your availability.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

Thanks Marcus — this looks great and aligns with our internal timelines.

Quick notes from Novanet side:
- I'm Novanet's engineering lead for this engagement (cc'd Tom Wu from infra).
- Procurement will pick up once we agree commercial terms; I've looped procurement@novanet.com to start tracking.
- For milestone 1, our initial target is 30 QPS (95th percentile latency <= 250ms) for the baseline model; goal after tuning is 45–50 QPS. We need the MAP to call out region as us-west only for now.

We can do the 10:00 PT sync. I'll have sample inference payloads ready and a short doc describing dataset size.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lena Park <lena@novanet.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Kickoff — GPU pool evaluation & close plan (Novanet)

Thanks — confirming the role. A couple of clarifications from product/eval side:
- Eval plan: we'll run three phases: baseline (stock model, default quant), tuned (quant + batching + cache), and stress (sustained load for 1 hour at target QPS).
- Key metrics: median latency, 95th latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1k tokens estimate.
- I recommend we set a hard SLO of 95th latency <= 300ms for the tuned run to be considered successful (we can tighten later).

Risk: if Novanet requires >8k token sequences consistently, that will change kernel selection — call that out as a risk in MAP.

Grace
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena@novanet.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Kickoff — GPU pool evaluation & close plan (Novanet)

Adding a few infra notes from the SRE side:
- For the pilot, I'll provision a dedicated pool with mixed A100/RTX capacity to match Novanet's target throughput. We should start with 4x A100-equivalent nodes for the initial tuned runs; can scale up if stress run shows bottlenecks.
- We'll test two batch size profiles: low-latency (batch=8) and high-throughput (batch=64) and capture token/latency tradeoffs.
- Attachment: throughput-baseline.csv (sample of expected QPS/latency under the stock config).

Constraint: procurement lead times for reserved capacity can be 3–4 weeks if Novanet needs a firm commit; we should surface a temporary burst policy for the pilot so they can avoid committing immediately.

Rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
